message:
validate policy against nodes, error if not valid

this commit aims to improve the feedback of "runtime" policy
errors which would only manifest when the rules are compiled to
filter rules with nodes.

this change will in;

file-based mode load the nodes from the db and try to compile the rules on
start up and return an error if they would not work as intended.

database-based mode prevent a new ACL being written to the database if
it does not compile with the current set of node.

Fixes #2073
Fixes #2044

Signed-off-by: Kristoffer Dalby <kristoffer@tailscale.com>

## PR summary

The pull request titled "validate policy against nodes, error if not valid" by user kradalby aims to enhance the feedback mechanism for "runtime" policy errors that occur when rules are compiled to filter rules with nodes. The proposed changes include two main functionalities:

1. In file-based mode, the system will load nodes from the database during startup and attempt to compile the rules. If the rules do not compile correctly, an error will be returned, providing immediate feedback on potential issues.

2. In database-based mode, the system will prevent the writing of a new Access Control List (ACL) to the database if it fails to compile with the current set of nodes, thereby ensuring that only valid policies are applied.

This pull request addresses issues #2073 and #2044, which relate to runtime errors and policy validation, respectively.

## Objectives from linked issues

The linked issues provide context for the need for improved policy validation in Headscale:

### Issue #2073
This issue reports a bug where users encounter an error message stating "Could not get the create map update" when attempting to register a node. The error occurs during the registration process, specifically when using the command `tailscale up`. The expected behavior is for the node to register and connect correctly to the network. The issue highlights the need for better error handling and feedback during node registration.

### Issue #2044
This feature request suggests implementing a validation step for the Headscale policy set command before applying any new policies. The user experienced a significant issue when a syntax error in the policy caused all clients to disconnect from the network. The request emphasizes the importance of validating ACL syntax to prevent such disruptions, proposing that the system should only load policies that pass validation checks. The user is willing to contribute to the design and implementation of this feature.
